-- The TARGET is these definitions, which also appear in the context: d14
def d14 (N : S1 X Y) (T : ℕ) : S1 X Y where
  A1 := Fin T × N.A1
  a2 := inferInstance
  A3 := fun a => N.A3 a.2
  a4 := fun a => N.a4 a.2
  a5 := fun a σ x =>
    N.a5 a.2 (fun m => if h : a.1.val = 0 then N.a4 m else σ (⟨a.1.val - 1, by omega⟩, m)) x
  a6 := fun σ =>
    if h : T = 0 then N.a6 N.a4 else N.a6 (fun m => σ (⟨T - 1, by omega⟩, m))
a_raw: {"translation": "For arbitrary types X and Y, d14 (defined in namespace S1) takes a record N of type S1 X Y and a natural number T, and constructs a new record of type S1 X Y with the following fields: (1) A1 is the product type Fin T × N.A1, consisting of pairs (k, n) where k is a natural number in 0, ..., T - 1 (so A1 is empty when T = 0) and n is in N.A1; (2) a2 is the automatically inferred proof that Fin T × N.A1 is finite (from the finiteness of Fin T and N.A1); (3) A3 sends each pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1 to the type N.A3 n, depending only on the second component n; (4) a4 sends each pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1 to the element N.a4 n of N.A3 n, again depending only on n; (5) a5 takes a pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1, a dependent function σ assigning to every pair (j, m) in Fin T × N.A1 an element of N.A3 m, and an element x of X, and returns N.a5 n τ x in N.A3 n, where τ : (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m is defined for each m in N.A1 to be N.a4 m if k.val = 0 (so σ is ignored when k.val = 0), and σ (k.val - 1, m) (with k.val - 1 regarded as an element of Fin T) if k.val ≠ 0; (6) a6 takes a dependent function σ assigning to every pair (j, m) in Fin T × N.A1 an element of N.A3 m, and returns an element of Y equal to N.a6 N.a4 if T = 0 (ignoring σ), and equal to N.a6 applied to the function m ↦ σ (T - 1, m) (with T - 1 regarded as an element of Fin T) if T ≠ 0. No hypotheses on X, Y, N, or T are required beyond their types; in particular, T = 0 is permitted and handled explicitly in a6."}
translation: For arbitrary types X and Y, d14 (defined in namespace S1) takes a record N of type S1 X Y and a natural number T, and constructs a new record of type S1 X Y with the following fields: (1) A1 is the product type Fin T × N.A1, consisting of pairs (k, n) where k is a natural number in 0, ..., T - 1 (so A1 is empty when T = 0) and n is in N.A1; (2) a2 is the automatically inferred proof that Fin T × N.A1 is finite (from the finiteness of Fin T and N.A1); (3) A3 sends each pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1 to the type N.A3 n, depending only on the second component n; (4) a4 sends each pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1 to the element N.a4 n of N.A3 n, again depending only on n; (5) a5 takes a pair (k, n) in Fin T × N.A1, a dependent function σ assigning to every pair (j, m) in Fin T × N.A1 an element of N.A3 m, and an element x of X, and returns N.a5 n τ x in N.A3 n, where τ : (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m is defined for each m in N.A1 to be N.a4 m if k.val = 0 (so σ is ignored when k.val = 0), and σ (k.val - 1, m) (with k.val - 1 regarded as an element of Fin T) if k.val ≠ 0; (6) a6 takes a dependent function σ assigning to every pair (j, m) in Fin T × N.A1 an element of N.A3 m, and returns an element of Y equal to N.a6 N.a4 if T = 0 (ignoring σ), and equal to N.a6 applied to the function m ↦ σ (T - 1, m) (with T - 1 regarded as an element of Fin T) if T ≠ 0. No hypotheses on X, Y, N, or T are required beyond their types; in particular, T = 0 is permitted and handled explicitly in a6.

divergences.description: In [P-H10], unrolling through time treats timesteps sequentially so that copy 1 carries out timestep 1 and passes its result to copy 2 for timestep 2, etc. (as in standard ML unrolling where each copy is dedicated to a fixed timestep). In d14 (as a declared modeling choice to stay within the synchronous S1 X Y type), all T copies run simultaneously at every timestep and every copy receives the current input x; consequently, copy 0 recomputes from N.a4 on every step rather than holding timestep 1's state, and for input sequences of length L < T the readout from copy T - 1 is computed along a chain starting from the initial state of copy T - L rather than from copy 0. This is harmless because it preserves acyclicity, size T * |N|, and input-output equivalence to N for all sequences of length ≤ T.

d14 takes an explicit finite horizon T : ℕ, so the unfolded network only agrees with N on input sequences of length ≤ T; if run on sequences longer than T, it computes N's output on a sliding window of the last T inputs rather than the full history (and for T = 0, it uses an empty node set with a special-case constant readout N.a6 N.a4). While [P-H10] explicitly considers fixed finite horizons (e.g., 100 timesteps), [P-D52a] states unfolding more broadly as implementing the same function without explicitly stating a horizon bound.

judgement.summary: d14 faithfully captures unrolling a network into T feedforward copies of N that preserve N's behavior up to T steps, with minor modeling caveats: the copies run synchronously in a real-time pipeline receiving the current input at every step (a declared choice), and equivalence is parameterized by an explicit finite horizon T (with sliding-window behavior beyond T steps and a special-case readout at T = 0).
